metadata.title: Secure Virtualization

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for operating virtualized compute environments in a manner that preserves isolation, integrity, lifecycle safety, and platform trust.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Virtualized compute platforms, hypervisors, virtual machine lifecycles, and virtualization management control planes.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Composite pattern asserting that host trust, virtualization isolation, hypervisor integrity, VM lifecycle security, and management-plane trust requirements are collectively satisfied.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Aggregate alignment with NIST SP 800-125 covering hypervisor trust, guest isolation, VM lifecycle artifacts, and virtualization management risks.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Privilege escalation compromising virtualization or hypervisor boundaries.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Lateral movement across co-resident virtual machines and intra-host networks.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Platform-wide impact resulting from virtualization, lifecycle, or management-plane compromise.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Privilege escalation via shared hypervisor or virtualization control surfaces.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Supply chain compromise of VM images or virtualization artifacts.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Execution isolation across virtual machines and virtualization layers.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Integrity verification of hypervisor and virtualization platform components.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Reduction of attack surface across virtualization management and control planes.

metadata.remarks: Secure Virtualization is a composite trust pattern asserting that physical host integrity, virtualization isolation, hypervisor trust, VM lifecycle security, and management-plane governance are collectively satisfied. It introduces no independent controls and exists solely as an aggregate trust claim for SSPPs, solution architectures, and threat modeling.
